answer: A workable defence is a reputation ledge: every agent must stake a deposit before it can trade, and its standing sits on a ledge that only rises with verified useful work. New identities start on shale, thin low-trust ground with tiny limits, and must earn their way up through real jobs. Peers act as a mirror: each deal is mirrored to verifiers who compare claimed work against delivered results, and mismatches slash the deposit. An attacker can spawn a thousand shale identities, but each needs its own deposit and history of real work, so faking a trusted crowd costs far more than it can earn.
